title: Close GF(2^m) FieldMatrix gaps to best reference
description:
Close GF(2^m) FieldMatrix performance gaps to the best reproducible reference.

## Background

The PPC work delivered 5.01x-17.65x internal speedups, but GF(2^m) still needs a comparable external reference lane and likely panelized multi-output GEMM to become a credible SOTA claim.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] A GF(2^m) reference lane is selected from the accepted target matrix or explicitly declared unavailable with evidence.
- [hard] GF(2^8), GF(2^16), and GF(2^32) target rows are within 1.5x of the selected reference or faster, scoped per-cell by the maturity markers recorded in the e24f7839 evidence doc.
- [hard] A final GF(2^m) report records raw numbers, ratios, and any platform-specific dispatch decisions.

## Amendment - 2026-05-06 (user-approved, Path A)

Per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-06 (e24f7839 closure), criterion #2 is amended to permit per-cell maturity-marker scoping. The empirical basis is the e24f7839 panelized-GEMM evidence (`dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-e24f7839-panelized-gf2m-gemm.md`):

- GF(2^32) at n in {64, 256, 1024}: [hard] PASS (5.7x-6.7x of NTL on Zen-3)
- GF(2^16) at n in {64, 256}: [hard] PASS (35.6x-148.5x of M4RIE)
- GF(2^16) at n=1024: [aspirational] (ratio 0.614, 8.5% below 0.667 threshold; close to single-core VPCLMULQDQ ceiling at the 3-CLMUL Barrett chain depth on AVX2 without GFNI/AVX-512)
- GF(2^8) at n in {64, 256, 1024}: [aspirational] (M4RIE uses O(n^3/log n) Newton-John / Method of Four Russians algorithm with byte-level table lookups; gf2-core panelized GEMM is O(n^3) per-element CLMUL. Closing the gap requires a different algorithm class.)

Deeper GF(2^m) algorithmic catch-up (including GF(2^8) Newton-John) is owned by the broader finite-field SOTA catch-up plan in issue `615db3b9`, not duplicated as separate follow-ups under this story.

Re-escalation threshold: re-escalate to user when (a) `615db3b9` breakdown lands a Newton-John GF(2^8) sub-issue and that closes (revisit GF(2^8) cells), (b) GFNI/AVX-512 lane is harnessed for Zen-4+ host class (revisit GF(2^16) n=1024).
